newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani rupee ends down in kerb, seen falling.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani rupee ends down in kerb, seen falling.

text.p: The Pakistani rupee ended 0.27 lower in the kerb market at 42.90 to the dollar on Monday as demand for the U.S. currency rose on fears that the central bank might depreciate the rupee soon, dealers said.
"Traders are buying the dollar as there is a general fear of a lower adjustment of the rupee," dealer Owais Kalia said.
The State (central) Bank of Pakistan rate, last changed on October 22, was 40.1200/40.3206 to the dollar.
The premium on the foreign exchange bearer certificates closed at 7.00 percent, compared to the opening at 6.25 percent.
